questions.topic: The Revelation and Preservation of al-Qur'an
questions.stem: The angel who brought the revelation of the Qur'an to Prophet Muhammad (SAW) was
questions.explanation: Angel Jibril (Gabriel) delivered the revelation from Allah.

questions.topic: The Revelation and Preservation of al-Qur'an
questions.stem: The first revelation came to the Prophet (SAW) in the Cave of
questions.explanation: He received the first verses while in the Cave of Hira near Makkah.

questions.topic: The Revelation and Preservation of al-Qur'an
questions.stem: The first verses of the Qur'an to be revealed begin with the word
questions.explanation: The first revelation was Qur'an 96:1-5, beginning "Iqra'".

questions.topic: The Revelation and Preservation of al-Qur'an
questions.stem: The Qur'an was revealed to the Prophet (SAW) over a period of about
questions.explanation: Revelation came gradually for about 23 years, in Makkah and Madinah.

questions.topic: The Revelation and Preservation of al-Qur'an
questions.stem: The Qur'an was first gathered into one book (mushaf) during the caliphate of
questions.explanation: After many memorisers died at Yamamah, Abu Bakr had Zaid bn Thabit collect the Qur'an.

questions.topic: The Revelation and Preservation of al-Qur'an
questions.stem: The Companion who headed the collection of the Qur'an into one volume was
questions.explanation: Zaid bn Thabit, a scribe of the Prophet (SAW), led the work.

questions.topic: The Revelation and Preservation of al-Qur'an
questions.stem: The caliph who made standard copies of the Qur'an and sent them to the main Muslim cities was
questions.explanation: Uthman had standard copies made so that all Muslims read the same text.

questions.topic: The Revelation and Preservation of al-Qur'an
questions.stem: How many surahs (chapters) are there in the Qur'an?
questions.explanation: The Qur'an has 114 surahs, arranged in 30 parts (juz').

questions.stem: Suratul Fatihah is also known as
questions.explanation: Al-Fatihah is called Ummul Kitab and must be recited in every raka'ah of salah.

questions.stem: In Suratul Fatihah, Muslims ask Allah to
options: guide them to the straight path
questions.explanation: "Ihdinas siratal mustaqim" means "Guide us to the straight path".

questions.stem: In Suratun Nas, Muslims seek refuge in Allah from
options: the evil of the whisperer who withdraws
questions.explanation: Suratun Nas seeks protection from the whispering of Shaytan among jinn and men.

questions.stem: Suratul Falaq seeks refuge with the Lord of
questions.explanation: Al-Falaq means the daybreak.

questions.stem: Which of these is mentioned in Suratul Falaq as something to seek refuge from?
options: The rich man when he boasts
questions.explanation: The surah ends with seeking refuge from the evil of the envier.

questions.stem: The main teaching of Suratul Ikhlas is
questions.explanation: Al-Ikhlas declares that Allah is One, Eternal, neither begets nor is begotten.

questions.stem: According to Suratul Ikhlas, Allah
questions.explanation: "Lam yalid wa lam yulad" — He begets not, nor is He begotten.

questions.stem: Suratul Masad condemns
questions.explanation: Abu Lahab, the Prophet's uncle, opposed Islam fiercely.

questions.stem: The lesson from Suratul Masad is that
options: family ties with the Prophet cannot save a person who opposes the truth
uncles must be obeyed in all things
questions.explanation: Abu Lahab's wealth and relationship did not save him.

questions.stem: Suratun Nasr speaks of a time when
options: people would enter the religion of Allah in crowds
questions.explanation: It refers to the help of Allah and victory, with people embracing Islam in large numbers.

questions.stem: At the time of victory, Suratun Nasr commands the Prophet (SAW) to
options: glorify Allah and seek His forgiveness
questions.explanation: Victory should lead to praise and humility, not pride.

questions.stem: Suratul Kafirun ends with "Lakum dinukum waliya din", meaning
options: "To you your religion and to me mine"
questions.explanation: This verse teaches religious tolerance without compromising one's faith.

questions.stem: Suratul Kawthar is the
questions.explanation: Al-Kawthar has only three short verses.

questions.stem: In Suratul Kawthar, Allah commands the Prophet (SAW) to
options: pray to his Lord and sacrifice
questions.explanation: "Fasalli li rabbika wanhar" — so pray to your Lord and sacrifice.

questions.stem: According to Suratul Ma'un, one who denies the religion is the one who
options: repulses the orphan and does not encourage feeding the poor
questions.explanation: The surah links true faith with caring for orphans and the needy.

questions.stem: Suratul Ma'un warns those who pray but
options: are heedless of their prayers and do good only to be seen
questions.explanation: It condemns showing off (riya') and refusing small kindnesses.

questions.stem: Suratu Quraysh mentions the trading journeys of the Quraysh during
questions.explanation: Allah reminds Quraysh of their safe winter and summer caravans.

questions.stem: Suratul Fil tells the story of the army that attacked the Ka'bah with
questions.explanation: Abrahah's army came with elephants to destroy the Ka'bah.

questions.stem: Allah destroyed the army of the elephant by sending
options: flocks of birds that pelted them with stones of baked clay
an army of angels on horses
questions.explanation: The birds (ababil) threw stones of baked clay (sijjil).

questions.stem: Suratul Humazah warns against
questions.explanation: Woe to every slanderer who gathers wealth and counts it.

questions.stem: According to Suratul 'Asr, mankind is in loss except those who
options: believe, do righteous deeds and advise one another to truth and patience
questions.explanation: The surah gives four qualities that save a person from loss.

questions.stem: In Suratul 'Asr, Allah swears by
questions.explanation: Al-'Asr means time; it teaches the value of time.

questions.stem: Suratut Takathur warns people who are distracted by
options: competition in piling up worldly things
questions.explanation: Rivalry for more wealth distracts people until they reach the graves.

questions.stem: Suratul Qari'ah teaches that on the Day of Judgement, a person whose scales are heavy with good deeds will
questions.explanation: Heavy scales lead to a pleasing life; light scales lead to the blazing fire.

questions.stem: In Suratut Tin, Allah swears by the fig, the olive, Mount Sinai and
questions.explanation: Al-Baladil Amin refers to Makkah.

questions.stem: Suratut Tin says Allah created man in
questions.explanation: "Laqad khalaqnal insana fi ahsani taqwim."

questions.stem: Suratush Sharh repeats the promise that with hardship there is
questions.explanation: "Fa inna ma'al 'usri yusra" — with hardship comes ease.

questions.stem: Suratud Duha commands the Prophet (SAW) not to oppress the orphan and not to
options: repel the one who asks (the beggar)
questions.explanation: The surah teaches kindness to orphans and those in need.

questions.stem: Suratud Duha was revealed to comfort the Prophet (SAW) when
options: revelation had paused for a while
questions.explanation: Allah assured him: "Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor does He hate you."

questions.stem: Taharah in Islam means
questions.explanation: Taharah is purification of the body, clothes and place, needed before worship.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a means of Taharah?
questions.explanation: Wudu, Ghusl and Tayammum are forms of purification; Salah is prayer that requires purification.

questions.topic: Performance of Ablution (al-Wudu) and things that vitiate it
questions.stem: Which of these nullifies (breaks) wudu?
questions.explanation: Anything that comes out of the private parts, such as wind, breaks wudu.

questions.topic: Performance of Ablution (al-Wudu) and things that vitiate it
questions.stem: In wudu, the arms are washed up to and including the
questions.explanation: Qur'an 5:6 commands washing the hands up to the elbows.

questions.topic: Performance of Ablution (al-Wudu) and things that vitiate it
questions.stem: Musa fell into a deep sleep while lying down after making wudu. Before praying he should
options: perform tayammum even though water is available
questions.explanation: Deep sleep breaks wudu, so it must be renewed.

questions.stem: Tayammum is performed with
questions.explanation: Tayammum uses clean earth when water is not available or cannot be used (Qur'an 5:6).

questions.stem: Tayammum is allowed when
options: water is not available or using it would harm a sick person
the weather is cold but water is available and safe
one is too lazy to fetch water
questions.explanation: It is a concession for genuine lack of water or illness.

questions.stem: A traveller performed tayammum because there was no water. Before praying, he finds clean water nearby. His tayammum
options: becomes invalid and he should perform wudu
remains valid for the whole day
questions.explanation: Finding water before prayer cancels tayammum.

questions.stem: Ghusl is compulsory for a Muslim woman
options: at the end of her menstrual period
questions.explanation: Ghusl is required after janabah, menstruation and post-natal bleeding.

questions.stem: In ghusl, a Muslim must
options: wash the whole body with water
strike the earth with the hands
questions.explanation: Ghusl is a full ritual bath covering the whole body.

questions.stem: The person who calls the adhan is called the
questions.explanation: The mu'adhdhin calls the faithful to prayer.

questions.stem: The first mu'adhdhin in Islam was
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) chose Bilal for his beautiful voice.

questions.stem: The iqamah is said
options: just before the congregational prayer begins
questions.explanation: Iqamah tells worshippers that the prayer is starting.

questions.stem: The phrase "As-salatu khairun minan naum" (prayer is better than sleep) is added to the adhan for
questions.explanation: It is said in the dawn adhan only.

questions.stem: How many raka'at are in the Maghrib prayer?
questions.explanation: Subh has 2, Zuhr 4, 'Asr 4, Maghrib 3 and 'Isha 4.

questions.stem: The total number of obligatory raka'at in the five daily prayers is
questions.explanation: Subh 2 + Zuhr 4 + 'Asr 4 + Maghrib 3 + 'Isha 4 = 17.

questions.stem: Salah begins with the opening takbir, which is
questions.explanation: Takbiratul ihram (Allahu Akbar) opens the prayer; it ends with taslim.

questions.stem: At-Tashahhud is recited while
questions.explanation: It is recited in the sitting position after the second and final raka'ah.

questions.stem: At-Tashahhud contains
options: the full text of Suratul Baqarah
the testimony that there is no god but Allah and Muhammad is His servant and messenger
the words of the adhan only
questions.explanation: Tashahhud comes from "shahadah", meaning bearing witness.

questions.stem: The person who leads a congregational prayer is called the
questions.explanation: The imam leads, and the followers (ma'mum) follow him.

questions.stem: According to a hadith, prayer in congregation is better than praying alone by
questions.explanation: Reported in Bukhari and Muslim from Ibn Umar.

questions.stem: Which of these prayers is performed without ruku' and sujud?
questions.explanation: The funeral prayer is said standing, with four takbirs.

questions.stem: The special prayer offered on Friday in place of Zuhr is
questions.explanation: Jumu'ah is two raka'at with a sermon (khutbah) on Friday.

questions.stem: Salatul Istisqa' is a special prayer for
questions.explanation: Muslims pray Istisqa' to ask Allah for rain during drought.

questions.stem: The Maghrib prayer is observed
questions.explanation: Maghrib time begins when the sun has set.

questions.stem: Qur'an 4:103 teaches that salah has been prescribed for believers at
questions.explanation: "Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers at specified times."

questions.stem: The Prophet (SAW) performed the Farewell Pilgrimage in
questions.explanation: Hajjatul Wada' took place in 10 A.H. (632 C.E.), shortly before his death.

questions.stem: Which teaching was part of the Prophet's Farewell Sermon?
options: An Arab has no superiority over a non-Arab except by piety
questions.explanation: The sermon stressed equality, the rights of women and the forbidding of usury.

questions.stem: Sujud Sahwi is
options: the prostration of forgetfulness made to correct mistakes in salah
the prostration made when reading the Qur'an
the first prostration in every prayer
questions.explanation: It is two prostrations made when a worshipper adds to or omits something in salah.

questions.stem: How many prostrations are made in Sujud Sahwi?
questions.explanation: Sujud Sahwi is two prostrations, made before or after the taslim depending on the mistake.

questions.stem: Hajj is performed in the Islamic month of
questions.explanation: The rites of Hajj take place from the 8th to the 13th of Dhul Hijjah.

questions.stem: The most important day of Hajj, when pilgrims stand at Arafat, is the
questions.explanation: The Prophet (SAW) said "Hajj is Arafah".

questions.stem: Walking seven times between Safa and Marwah during Hajj is called
questions.explanation: Sa'y remembers Hajar's search for water for Isma'il.

questions.stem: Hajj is obligatory once in a lifetime on every Muslim who is
options: adult, sane and physically and financially able
questions.explanation: Qur'an 3:97 requires Hajj of those who are able to make the journey.

questions.stem: The gift that a husband must give to his bride in Islamic marriage is called
questions.explanation: Mahr is the bride's right (Qur'an 4:4).

questions.stem: Which of these is required for a valid Islamic marriage?
questions.explanation: An Islamic marriage needs the guardian (wali), mahr, witnesses and offer and acceptance.

questions.stem: The Qur'an (2:233) recommends that mothers breastfeed their children for
questions.explanation: Breastfeeding for two years also helps to space births.

questions.stem: In Islam, family planning mainly means
options: refusing to have any children forever
spacing births so parents can care well for mother and children
having as many children as possible without care
questions.explanation: Islam allows spacing of children but forbids killing children for fear of poverty (Qur'an 17:31).

questions.stem: The word "Islam" means
options: submission to the will of Allah and peace
questions.explanation: Islam means peaceful submission to Allah; a Muslim is one who submits.

questions.stem: According to Qur'an 51:56, Allah created jinn and mankind
questions.explanation: "I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me."

questions.stem: The Kalimatush Shahadah is "La ilaha illallah, Muhammadur Rasulullah", meaning
options: Allah is the greatest; prayer is better than sleep
In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful
There is no god but Allah; Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah
All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds
questions.explanation: It is the declaration of faith that makes a person a Muslim.

questions.stem: The first part of the Shahadah, "La ilaha illallah", rejects
options: the worship of anything besides Allah
questions.explanation: It negates all false gods and affirms Allah alone.

questions.stem: Which of these is one of the five pillars of Islam?
questions.explanation: The pillars are Shahadah, Salah, Zakah, Sawm and Hajj.

questions.stem: Fasting in the month of Ramadan is called
questions.explanation: Sawm is the fourth pillar of Islam.

questions.stem: How many articles of faith (Arkanul Iman) are there in Islam?
questions.explanation: Belief in Allah, angels, books, messengers, the Last Day and divine decree.

questions.topic: The Beautiful Names of Allah (Asma'ul Husna) I
questions.stem: In Qur'an 59:23, the name "Al-Quddus" means
questions.explanation: Al-Quddus means the Holy One, free from all defects.

questions.topic: The Beautiful Names of Allah (Asma'ul Husna) I
questions.stem: Which of these names of Allah is found in Qur'an 59:23?
questions.explanation: Qur'an 59:23 includes Al-Malik, Al-Quddus, As-Salam, Al-Mu'min and Al-Muhaymin.

questions.topic: The Beautiful Names of Allah (Asma'ul Husna) I
questions.stem: The name "Al-Malik" means
questions.explanation: Al-Malik means the absolute King and Owner of all.

questions.topic: The Beautiful Names of Allah (Asma'ul Husna) II
questions.stem: Qur'an 59:24 describes Allah as Al-Khaliq, meaning
questions.explanation: Al-Khaliq is the One who creates from nothing.

questions.topic: The Beautiful Names of Allah (Asma'ul Husna) II
questions.stem: In Qur'an 59:24, "Al-Musawwir" means
questions.explanation: Al-Musawwir gives every creature its shape and form.

questions.topic: The Beautiful Names of Allah (Asma'ul Husna) III
questions.stem: The names "Ar-Rahman" and "Ar-Rahim" describe Allah as
questions.explanation: They are mentioned in the Bismillah and in Suratul Fatihah.

questions.topic: The Beautiful Names of Allah (Asma'ul Husna) IV
questions.stem: The name "Ar-Razzaq" means
questions.explanation: Ar-Razzaq is the One who provides sustenance for all creatures.

questions.topic: The Beautiful Names of Allah (Asma'ul Husna) IV
questions.stem: A Muslim who sins and repents hopes in Allah as "Al-Ghafur", meaning
questions.explanation: Al-Ghafur forgives the sins of those who repent.

questions.topic: The Beautiful Names of Allah (Asma'ul Husna) V
questions.stem: The name "Al-'Alim" means
questions.explanation: Al-'Alim knows everything, open and hidden.

questions.topic: The Beautiful Names of Allah (Asma'ul Husna) V
questions.stem: Knowing that Allah is "As-Sami'" (All-Hearing) and "Al-Basir" (All-Seeing) should make a Muslim
options: careful about what he says and does even in secret
questions.explanation: Since Allah hears and sees all, a believer guards his conduct at all times.

questions.stem: Prophet Muhammad (SAW) is called "Khatamun Nabiyyin", meaning
options: the one who spoke to Allah
questions.explanation: Qur'an 33:40 states that he is the last Prophet.

questions.stem: How many prophets are mentioned by name in the Qur'an?
questions.explanation: The Qur'an names 25 prophets, from Adam to Muhammad (SAW).

questions.stem: Angels were created from
questions.explanation: Angels were created from light, jinn from fire and Adam from clay (Sahih Muslim).

questions.stem: The angel who will blow the trumpet on the Last Day is
questions.explanation: Israfil will sound the trumpet to announce the Day of Resurrection.

questions.stem: The angels who question the dead in the grave are
questions.explanation: Munkar and Nakir ask about one's Lord, religion and Prophet.

questions.stem: The angels who record a person's good and bad deeds are
questions.explanation: Qur'an 50:18 mentions Raqib and 'Atid as watchful recorders.

questions.stem: Al-Qada wal-Qadar refers to belief in
questions.explanation: It is the sixth article of faith: everything happens by Allah's knowledge and decree.

questions.stem: Aisha failed her examination because she did not study, and she said, "It is Allah's decree." In Islam, belief in Qadar
options: does not remove a person's duty to make effort
means results do not depend on deeds
questions.explanation: A Muslim must strive and then trust Allah; Qadar is not an excuse for laziness.

questions.topic: The Meaning and Importance of Hadith
questions.stem: Hadith refers to
options: the words of Allah revealed through Jibril
the sayings, actions and approvals of Prophet Muhammad (SAW)
questions.explanation: Hadith records what the Prophet said, did or approved.

questions.topic: The Meaning and Importance of Hadith
questions.stem: Hadith is important to Muslims mainly because it
options: contains only stories of earlier prophets
is recited in every raka'ah of salah
explains and gives details of the teachings of the Qur'an
questions.explanation: For example, the Qur'an commands salah and the Hadith shows how to perform it.

questions.topic: The Meaning and Importance of Hadith
questions.stem: A Hadith in which the Prophet (SAW) reports the meaning from Allah in his own words is called
questions.explanation: In Hadith Qudsi, the meaning is from Allah while the wording is the Prophet's.

questions.stem: The chain of narrators of a Hadith is called the
questions.explanation: The isnad is the chain; the matn is the actual text.

questions.stem: The Companion who reported the largest number of Hadith is
questions.explanation: Abu Hurairah narrated over five thousand Hadith.

questions.stem: Hadith are graded into three main kinds according to their reliability:
questions.explanation: Sahih is sound, Hasan is good and Da'if is weak.

questions.stem: Among the wives of the Prophet (SAW), the one who reported the most Hadith was
questions.explanation: Aishah bint Abi Bakr reported over two thousand Hadith.

questions.topic: The Preservation and Collection of Hadith
questions.stem: The most famous collection of authentic Hadith was compiled by
questions.explanation: Sahih al-Bukhari is regarded as the most authentic Hadith collection.

questions.topic: The Preservation and Collection of Hadith
questions.stem: Which of these is one of the six authentic collections (As-Sihahus Sittah)?
questions.explanation: The six are Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, Tirmidhi, Nasa'i and Ibn Majah.

questions.topic: The Preservation and Collection of Hadith
questions.stem: The Umayyad caliph who ordered the official writing down of Hadith was
questions.explanation: Umar bn Abdul Aziz feared the Hadith would be lost as scholars died.

questions.topic: The Preservation and Collection of Hadith
questions.stem: The collection "Forty Hadith" (Al-Arba'un) was compiled by
questions.explanation: Imam Yahya bn Sharaf an-Nawawi compiled the famous Forty Hadith.

questions.stem: Hadith No. 1 of An-Nawawi teaches that "actions are judged by
questions.explanation: Innamal a'malu binniyyat — the value of a deed depends on its intention.

questions.stem: Hadith No. 1 of An-Nawawi was narrated by
questions.explanation: Umar reported it; it is in Bukhari and Muslim.

questions.stem: Hadith No. 2 of An-Nawawi tells of a man in very white clothes who asked the Prophet about Islam, Iman, Ihsan and the Hour. The man was
questions.explanation: The Prophet said, "That was Jibril, who came to teach you your religion."

questions.stem: In Hadith No. 2, Ihsan is defined as
options: worshipping Allah as though you see Him, for though you do not see Him, He sees you
questions.explanation: Ihsan is excellence and sincerity in worship.

questions.stem: Hadith No. 3 of An-Nawawi teaches that Islam is built on
questions.explanation: Shahadah, Salah, Zakah, Hajj and Sawm.

questions.stem: Hadith No. 4 of An-Nawawi describes
options: the night journey of the Prophet
the story of the people of the elephant
the stages of the creation of a person in the mother's womb and the writing of his destiny
questions.explanation: An angel is sent to breathe in the soul and write his provision, life span, deeds and fate.

questions.stem: Hadith No. 5 teaches that whoever introduces into Islam something that is not part of it
questions.explanation: It warns against innovation (bid'ah) in religion; narrated by Aishah.

questions.stem: Hadith No. 6 says, "The halal is clear and the haram is clear, and between them are
questions.explanation: A Muslim should avoid doubtful things to protect his religion and honour.

questions.stem: Hadith No. 6 says there is a piece of flesh in the body which, if it is sound, the whole body is sound. This is the
questions.explanation: The heart controls a person's actions.

questions.stem: Hadith No. 7 of An-Nawawi teaches that "religion is
questions.explanation: Ad-dinun nasihah — religion is sincerity towards Allah, His Book, His Messenger, leaders and the people.

questions.stem: Hadith No. 8 of An-Nawawi states that a person's life and wealth are protected once he
options: testifies to the Oneness of Allah, establishes salah and pays zakah
questions.explanation: Narrated by Ibn Umar, it links the shahadah with prayer and zakah.

questions.stem: Hadith No. 9 teaches: "What I have forbidden you, avoid; and what I have commanded you, do
options: as much as you are able"
questions.explanation: Islam does not burden a person beyond his ability.

questions.stem: Hadith No. 10 teaches that "Allah is good and accepts only
questions.explanation: Earning and spending must be lawful (halal) for prayers to be accepted.

questions.stem: Hadith No. 11 advises: "Leave that which makes you doubt for
options: that which does not make you doubt"
questions.explanation: Narrated by al-Hasan bn Ali, it teaches caution in doubtful matters.

questions.stem: According to Hadith No. 12, part of the excellence of a person's Islam is
options: leaving alone what does not concern him
questions.explanation: Avoiding unnecessary matters and gossip shows good faith.

questions.stem: Hadith No. 13: "None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he
questions.explanation: Narrated by Anas bn Malik; it teaches brotherhood and unselfishness.

questions.stem: Hadith No. 14 of An-Nawawi teaches that
options: it is lawful to kill an enemy anywhere
blood relatives must be obeyed in all things
the blood of a Muslim is sacred and may be taken only in cases laid down by Islamic law
questions.explanation: It stresses the sanctity of life; only a lawful court may punish in the stated cases.

questions.stem: Hadith No. 15 says whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should
questions.explanation: It also commands honouring one's neighbour and guest.

questions.stem: Which pair of duties is mentioned in Hadith No. 15?
options: Honouring the neighbour and honouring the guest
questions.explanation: Faith shows itself in good speech and generosity to neighbours and guests.

questions.stem: A man asked the Prophet (SAW) for advice and he repeatedly said, "Do not
questions.explanation: Hadith No. 16 teaches self-control over anger.

questions.stem: Hadith No. 17 teaches that when slaughtering an animal, a Muslim should
options: sharpen the blade and spare the animal suffering
slaughter it in front of other animals for fun
questions.explanation: Allah has prescribed ihsan (excellence) in everything, even in slaughter.

questions.stem: Hadith No. 23 begins, "Purity (cleanliness) is
questions.explanation: At-tuhuru shatrul iman — cleanliness is half of faith.

questions.stem: Hadith No. 24 is a Hadith Qudsi in which Allah says, "O My servants, I have forbidden
options: oppression (injustice) for Myself and made it forbidden among you"
questions.explanation: Muslims must not oppress one another.

questions.stem: In Hadith No. 25, poor Companions complained that the rich got more reward. The Prophet (SAW) taught that
options: every tasbih, takbir and good deed is a charity
the rich must give all their wealth away
questions.explanation: Even remembrance of Allah and good actions count as sadaqah.

questions.stem: According to Hadith No. 26, which of these is a form of charity?
options: Removing a harmful object from the road
questions.explanation: Helping a man onto his animal, a good word and removing harm are all charity.

questions.stem: Hadith No. 27 defines righteousness as good character, and sin as
options: what wavers in your soul and you dislike people to know about
questions.explanation: Narrated by an-Nawwas bn Sam'an; the conscience recognises sin.

questions.stem: The period in Arabia before Islam is known as
questions.explanation: It was marked by idol worship and many social evils.

questions.stem: Which of these practices was common in Arabia before Islam?
questions.explanation: Qur'an 81:8-9 condemns the burying of baby girls alive.

questions.stem: Before Islam, the Ka'bah was filled with
questions.explanation: There were about 360 idols in and around the Ka'bah.

questions.stem: Prophet Muhammad (SAW) was born in
questions.explanation: He was born in Makkah into the Quraysh tribe.

questions.stem: The Prophet (SAW) was born in the Year of the
questions.explanation: He was born in the year Abrahah attacked Makkah, about 570 C.E.

questions.stem: The father of the Prophet (SAW) was
questions.explanation: Abdullah died before the Prophet was born.

questions.stem: The woman who nursed the Prophet (SAW) in the desert as a baby was
questions.explanation: Halimah of the Banu Sa'd tribe was his foster-mother.

questions.stem: After his mother Aminah died, the young Prophet (SAW) was cared for first by
questions.explanation: He was later cared for by his uncle Abu Talib after Abdul Muttalib died.

questions.topic: The Prophet (SAW): His Youth and Marriage to Khadijah
questions.stem: Because of his honesty, the Prophet (SAW) was known in his youth as
questions.explanation: Even his enemies trusted him with their valuables.

questions.topic: The Prophet (SAW): His Youth and Marriage to Khadijah
questions.stem: The Prophet (SAW) married Khadijah when he was
questions.explanation: He was 25 and she was about 40.

questions.topic: The Prophet (SAW): His Youth and Marriage to Khadijah
questions.stem: Khadijah was impressed by the Prophet (SAW) mainly because
options: he was the richest man in Makkah
he was the king of Makkah
he managed her trade caravan to Syria with honesty and success
